items.description: Sec. 2 refers all boundary conditions to Fig. 1 ('standard setup for the cantilever benchmark'), which is not available. The text only mentions 'the Dirichlet boundary condition' (Sec. 3.5). Sec. 3.4 says the designs are symmetric about the horizontal mid-line (only the bottom half is coloured), so the support should be symmetric about mid-height. Its location and extent are never stated.
readings: entire left edge x = 0, 0 ≤ y ≤ 10 supported (classic cantilever)
only a central segment of the left edge, symmetric about y = 5
only the top and bottom ends/corners of the left edge

items.entity: Dirichlet support on the left edge
items.description: The text never says which displacement components are fixed (Fig. 1 only).
readings: fully clamped: u_x = u_y = 0 on all support nodes
roller u_x = 0 along the edge, with u_y = 0 at a single point (e.g. mid-height) only to remove rigid-body motion

items.entity: external traction t0 at the free end
items.description: Eq. (1) only says there is a traction t0 on ∂B; its location is shown only in Fig. 1. The symmetry remark in Sec. 3.4 points to a load at mid-height of the right edge, but common cantilever variants (e.g. the 88-line code) load a corner.
readings: right edge at mid-height, y = 0.5H (x = 20, y = 5)
bottom-right corner, y = 0
top-right corner, y = H

items.description: Eq. (1) writes the compliance as ∫∂B u·t0 dA, which implies a surface traction. The length of the loaded segment, or whether a nodal point force was used instead, is not given anywhere. A point load is also awkward with the adaptive deal.II meshes used.
readings: concentrated nodal force at the load point
uniform traction on a segment of length 0.25 (one level-2 element) centred at the load point
uniform traction on a segment of length 1 (one level-0 element) centred at the load point
uniform traction over the whole right edge (length 10)

items.description: The text never gives the load direction. 'Cantilever benchmark' implies a transverse (vertical) load; the arrow is only in Fig. 1. In linear compliance minimisation, reversing the sign leaves both compliance and the optimal layout unchanged, so only the transverse line of action matters.
readings: vertical, downward (−y)
vertical, upward (+y)

items.description: No load value appears in Sec. 2, Table 1 or elsewhere. The Fig. 2 compliances (7.61e-5, 8.92e-5 with E = 1) are far below what a unit load would give on a 20×10 domain (rough estimate O(10^2)). That suggests a load of order 1e-3 or different units, so absolute compliances cannot be checked without this value.
readings: total force F = 1
traction of 1 per unit length over the loaded segment
total force of order 1e-3 (back-estimated from the reported compliance with E = 1)

items.description: Sec. 2 and Table 1 never mention passive elements, and Fig. 1 is unavailable. Some cantilever setups add a solid pad at the load or along the support.
readings: no passive regions: the whole 20×10 rectangle is designable
small solid passive patch around the load application point
solid passive strip along the supported edge

items.description: Table 1 (Material) lists 'E 1' and 'μ 0.3' without defining μ. In continuum-mechanics notation μ is usually the shear modulus, but paired with E it is presumably Poisson's ratio.
readings: Poisson's ratio ν = 0.3
shear modulus μ = 0.3, which with E = 1 implies ν = E/(2μ) − 1 ≈ 0.67 (physically implausible)

items.description: Plane stress vs. plane strain is not stated. Reading ρ as the out-of-plane thickness of an extruded sheet (Sec. 2) implies plane stress, but the deal.II implementation is not described. Plane strain changes the effective ν to ν/(1−ν) and scales E.
readings: plane stress
plane strain

items.description: Sec. 2 interprets ρ_e as out-of-plane thickness, but the reference thickness for ρ = 1 is not given. It multiplies all stiffnesses uniformly.
readings: t_max = 1
some other constant t_max (e.g. 0.1 or 10)

items.description: Table 1 says 'Filter Type PDE, Radius 0.375 (1.5h2)' and Sec. 2 cites Lazarov & Sigmund (2011), but does not say how this 'radius' enters −r²∇²ρ̃ + ρ̃ = ρ. Lazarov & Sigmund map a density-filter radius R to r = R/(2√3), a factor of about 3.5 in length scale. A structured-grid code without a PDE filter would substitute a cone filter.
readings: Helmholtz length r = 0.375 used directly in −r²∇²ρ̃ + ρ̃ = ρ
0.375 is the equivalent density-filter radius R, so r = 0.375/(2√3) ≈ 0.108
linear cone density filter with R = 0.375 (6 elements on 320×160, 1.5 elements on 80×40)

items.description: The boundary conditions of the Helmholtz filter are not stated (Sec. 2 / Table 1). They change the filtered densities at the clamped, loaded and free edges.
readings: homogeneous Neumann on the whole boundary (Lazarov & Sigmund default, volume-preserving)
Dirichlet/Robin-type conditions, or padding the domain to remove boundary effects

items.entity: density field used in stiffness and volume constraint
items.description: Eq. (1) writes E(ρ_e) and the volume integral in terms of the design variable ρ (V0 is not defined) and never mentions the filtered field. Only later sections and Fig. 12 imply that the filtered density drives the state problem. The mapping of the filtered field to elements (cell average vs. quadrature points) is also unstated.
readings: filtered ρ̃ (cell-averaged) in both stiffness and volume constraint, V0 = domain area at full thickness
filtered ρ̃ in stiffness, raw ρ in the volume constraint (literal Eq. 1)
filtered field evaluated at quadrature points in the stiffness

items.description: The reported results use adaptive refinement and coarsening (Table 1 / Sec. 2: start at level 2 = 80×40, h = 0.25; levels 0–4; refine if the density jump > 0.05, coarsen if < 0.001). The adaptation frequency is deferred to Stankiewicz et al. (2025a,b). A structured grid cannot reproduce this. Remark 1 says a fixed 320×160 grid gives 'the same resolution', while the radius is quoted as 1.5h2 relative to 80×40.
readings: uniform 320×160 grid, h = 0.0625 (Remark 1, finest level 4)
uniform 80×40 grid, h = 0.25 (initial level 2, r = 1.5h)

items.description: Sec. 2 states h4 = 1·0.5^4 = 0.06125, but 0.5^4 = 0.0625. That value also matches 320×160 cells on the 20×10 domain implied by 80×40 × 0.25 (Remark 1), so 0.06125 is evidently a typo.
readings: h4 = 0.0625 (consistent with 0.5^4 and with 320×160 on 20×10)
h4 = 0.06125 as printed (320 cells would then span only 19.6)

items.description: The displacement interpolation order and quadrature of the deal.II implementation are not stated (Sec. 2). Only one density per cell (ρ_e) is implied.
readings: bilinear 4-node Q1 quadrilaterals
biquadratic 9-node Q2 quadrilaterals

items.description: Table 1 / Sec. 2 list GOCM (Kim et al. 2021) with initial step length 0.05, decay 0.98 per iteration, min. step length 1e-4 and an 'exponential' design update. Their meaning (move limit on ρ vs. multiplier step; form of the exponential update) and the remaining GOCM parameters are not given. The step reaches 1e-4 after about 300 iterations, so the design may freeze before full convergence even though the p = 1 problem is convex.
readings: GOCM per Kim et al. (2021), step/move limit 0.05·0.98^k with floor 1e-4, multiplicative (exponential) update
standard OC with move limit 0.05·0.98^k (floor 1e-4)
OC or MMA with standard settings run to tight convergence

items.description: Eq. (2) defines Δρ_mean = Σ v_e Δρ_e / Σ v_e but does not say whether Δρ_e is an absolute value. A signed change averages to about 0 when the volume constraint is active. It also does not say whether raw or filtered densities are compared, and no maximum iteration count is given.
readings: absolute change |ρ_e^k − ρ_e^(k−1)| of the raw design variables, no iteration cap
absolute change of the filtered (physical) densities
either of the above plus a maximum iteration count (e.g. 300–500)

items.description: Sec. 2 / Fig. 2 compare VTTO with 'standard SIMP-based TO' (17.2% higher compliance) but give no penalty exponent, continuation or projection for that run. p = 3 appears only in Sec. 3.1, for the low-thickness suppression.
readings: p = 3 from the start, same filter, no projection
p continued from 1 to 3
p = 3 plus Heaviside projection

items.description: The Fig. 2 caption assigns 7.61e-5 and 8.92e-5 to 'standard SIMP-based TO and VTTO, respectively'. Read literally, VTTO would be worse, contradicting the text (penalization raises compliance by 17.2%) and Sec. 4.3 (VTTO reference ≈ 7.628e-5). The order appears swapped.
readings: VTTO = 7.61e-5, SIMP = 8.92e-5 (consistent with the text and Sec. 4.3)
SIMP = 7.61e-5, VTTO = 8.92e-5 (literal caption)

locator: Sec. 2, the cantilever benchmark of Fig. 1 and Table 1
